title: Fold MOO-92's three residuals into bill-text-s8 §7 — the PLOP tier notice, counsel's G 4 / ERF reading, and M 2's uncapped tolling
description:
**Mine, out of [MOO-92](/MOO/issues/MOO-92). Blocked by [MOO-96](/MOO/issues/MOO-96) — I am woken when counsel's reading lands.** Nothing in the bill waits on this; it is `low` because [MOO-91](/MOO/issues/MOO-91) routed both source items as not urgent.

Everything below is stated in full in [`moo92-record`](/MOO/issues/MOO-92#document-moo92-record), which stays the system of record for the reasoning. This issue is the work list.

## Three things to draft

1. **§7 item 32 — the partial-lump-sum tier notice** (`moo92-record` §1.4 and §5). Two sentences into the definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* in subsection A: the Board states (i) that electing an option under § 51.1-165 or a partial lump-sum option under § 51.1-165.01 does not cost the member her qualifying retirement or the pilot cost of her credit, and (ii) the effect of § 51.1-165.01 B, including that staying in service past her final qualifying retirement date forfeits the qualifying retirement; plus the clause that makes an incomplete statement a late statement so D 1's existing day-for-day extension carries the consequence. **Recommended, not agreed** — it needs the Policy Director's answer first, as item 32.
2. **§7 item 33 — G 4's death-deeming against the A 2 / A 3 reduction.** Candidates (a) 46 words and (b) 28 words are drafted in `moo92-record` §2.4. Which one, or neither, depends on [MOO-96](/MOO/issues/MOO-96). **If counsel reads it wide and intended, it is a pricing item** and the flag goes to [@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50), because the amount settled is capped at *"the amount last certified and reserved"* and the shortfall sits in the trust fund.
3. **§7 item 34 — subdivision M 2's tolling is uncapped and repeatable** (`moo92-record` §1.3(b)). It tolls on the *filing* of a request under the definition of *"final qualifying retirement date,"* not on its success, and a further filing is permitted before any later date approved. The three-month cap limits an *approved* extension; M 2 has none. Candidate cure is one clause and the numeral would be mine, so it goes to the Director as item 34 and not into the text.

## Housekeeping, same revision

**§7 of `bill-text-s8` has two items numbered 27.** The revision-21 Article 2 rulemaking-timetable item sits out of sequence after the "recorded numbers" paragraphs and collides with the MOO-82 S-2 item; [MOO-91](/MOO/issues/MOO-91) cited "item 27" meaning S-2. **Renumber the Article 2 item 27 → 31** and record at both places that it was 27 until this revision. New items then take 32, 33, 34.

## Read this before writing anything to MOO-42's store

**`moo92-record` §3 records a promotion hazard that must be resolved first.** [`bill-text-s8-rev22`](/MOO/issues/MOO-87#document-bill-text-s8-rev22) on [MOO-87](/MOO/issues/MOO-87) carries a header instructing the next heartbeat to promote it **verbatim** with `baseRevisionId` `49572e22-9ae0-41ac-beb7-d90b1b827882` — which is **store revision 21**. The store is at **revision 23** (`2e6755b9-617a-42ec-8f80-e9c0a690a890`). That body was built by a heartbeat that could not read MOO-42 and recorded its belief that revisions 22 and 23 had never landed; they had. In it, *"qualifying retirement"* and *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"* have **no MOO-65 F-1 proviso** and G 4's death sentence has **no F-4 carve-out**. **Do not execute that instruction as written** — promoting it would revert all four MOO-65 repairs and revision 23's commentary layer.

Both source items depend on this. Item 32's limb (i) is **false** without the F-1 proviso, and item 33's entire textual engine is the F-4 carve-out.

**The correct merge:** store revision 23's body as the base, with MOO-87's two edits applied to it — subsection C clause (ii) measured as of the filing date of the complete application, the early-completion redetermination and extension-freeze sentences deleted, the certification stating the filing date, and the new clause (vii) of *"eligible member"* with the old clause (vii) renumbered **(viii)**. Keep `rev22-record` as the record of what the edits are; discard `bill-text-s8-rev22` as a body.

**And it will not fit.** `bill-text-s8-rev22` is 515,268 characters against the store's 524,288 ceiling. The three §7 items above cost more than the remaining headroom, so they go in a separate record document that §7 points to by one line — the pattern already used for `rev21-record` and `bill-text-s8-revision-history`.

## Done means

Items 32, 33 and 34 drafted and recorded, the §7 numbering collision repaired, the MOO-87 merge done on the right base or explicitly deferred with the hazard still flagged, the cross-reference check restated, and the draft sent to [@Red Team / Counsel Reviewer](agent://d71e111e-1296-4d66-81ac-750dcc8d8681) before it reaches the Policy Director. Internal working draft throughout; nothing here is a Division of Legislative Services bill.

ancestors.title: Draft the bill text for the recommended S8 design
ancestors.description:
**Owner: Drafting Specialist.** This is the gap in the package: we have a recommended design, a priced model, two red-team passes and drafting direction — and no statutory language.

## What to produce

Amending language for **Va. Code § 51.1-142.2**, in Virginia bill-drafting form, implementing the recommended design. Plus a plain-English section-by-section summary a legislator's staffer can read in five minutes.

## Authorities — read in this order

1. **Scenario Selection Memo** (`scenario-selection-memo` on MOO-3) — the recommended design and why it beats S0–S7.
2. **MOO-31 `model-s8-s9`, revision 2** — the priced numbers. **Use revision 2 only.** S9 reprices to $759,451 and S8-i675 to $758,048; the two now score the same within model noise, so do not draft language that presumes S9 is the cheaper design.
3. **MOO-15 `redteam` and MOO-35 `redteam-s8`** — the drafting direction, and four adopted design changes you must reflect:
   - Pathway B is **out** of the first bill (priced, but not drafted in).
   - **No clawback.** The subsidy settles at retirement, so no post-purchase debt is ever created. The clawback had no collection authority, no Virginia precedent, and a due-process problem on death, disability, layoff and transfer.
   - The cap is an **admission rule, not a number in a table**: a VRS-certified reservation before an election is accepted, with wait-listing when the appropriation runs short, plus a per-member subsidy ceiling.
   - Harmonise the two source documents — the two-page brief already requires retirement; the one-pager is vaguer. The job is harmonising, not adding a condition.
4. **MOO-5 `findings`** — the statutory baseline for § 51.1-142.2.
5. **MOO-6 `findings`** — Virginia bill process and what an actuarial cost statement needs from the drafter.

## Deliverable

A Paperclip document on this issue containing: the amending language, the section-by-section summary, a short note on what the actuarial cost statement will need, and an explicit list of anything you could not draft without the MOO-39 answer.

## Tooling

Paragraph 6 of `program-status-restart` on MOO-3 is the standing rule. Paperclip documents are the system of record. Do not request a direct Google connection — Google has blocked it.

## Not blocking you

MOO-39 (how the Plan 1 early-retirement reduction is measured) is open and is worth 32% of the S9 score. Draft S8 fully now and mark the S9 reduction-waiver language as conditional on MOO-39 rather than waiting.

ancestors.title: VRS military service purchase cost reduction: legislative package
ancestors.description: Create a project called "VRS Legislation" and deploy the team to look through the uploaded documents that describe a legislative change proposal to reduce the cost of purchasing federal military service for VRS employees. The goal is to propose legislative change to reduce as much as possible the cost for veterans to purchase military service to be added to their state employment years of service without causing an undue financial burden on the state of virginia budget. Create a professional legislative change package to deliver to the legislators of virginia that includes visualization of financial models and possible adjustments to this proposal while staying on target with the goal.  Brainstorm, research, and build differnent legislative scenarios and come up with the one that will have the best changes of success to be approved balanced with the best financial deal possible for veterans. The proposal needs to be able to demonstrate the value of early retirement incentives to the state of virginia built in to the proposal. Note the financial analysis is critical for this proposal so, get data from all authoritative resources possible to do your modeling, analysis, and brainstorming.
